newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: SOCCER SHOWCASE-PORTO BEAT BENFICA, TIGHTEN GRIP ON TITLE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-PORTO BEAT BENFICA, TIGHTEN GRIP ON TITLE.

text.p: Champions Porto tightened their grip on the title with an efficient 2-1 win over rivals Benfica on Saturday that widened their lead to eight points at the top of the Portuguese league.
Goals from Brazilian striker Mario Jardel and defender Jorge Costa, one in each half, were enough to sink a disappointing Benfica who lacked the confidence to launch any sustained attacks.

The home side managed only a brief period of dominance just after the start of the second half when captain Joao Vieira Pinto raised the hopes of local supporters in the 75,000 crowd after nipping in to head home.
Vieira Pinto's strike levelled the scores but Porto quickly restored their advantage with Costa scoring after Benfica goalkeeper Michel Preud'Homme failed to gather a fiercely struck free kick.

Although Porto manager Antonio Oliveira refused to accept that the victory virtually assured his team of a record-breaking third successive league title, Benfica now face a daunting task to make up ground on the leaders.
"It is just three more points, just one more victory. Nothing more, nothing less," said Oliveira in typically laconic style.
But Oliveira, who took over from former England manager Bobby Robson this season, did not hide his satisfaction at the way his side played.
"For what we did during the game and the fact that we had the better chances, we deserved to win," he said.
Porto moved ahead in the 23rd minute when Jardel, the league's top scorer with 13 goals, majestically controlled a cross from the right on his chest and volleyed past a helpless Preud'Homme.

Perhaps fearing a repeat of the 5-0 drubbing they received the last time Porto visited Lisbon's Stadium of Light last September in the final of the Portuguese Supercup, Benfica still did not press forward in strength even after going behind.
The nearest they came to scoring in the first half was from a free kick by Brazilian midfielder Valdo Filho which went just wide of the upright.

Porto could even feel aggrieved that they were not awarded a penalty in the 39th minute when Preud'Homme appeared to bring down Slovenian midfielder Zlatko Zahovic as he sought to round the goalkeeper.
For Benfica, Vieira Pinto was always dangerous but the home side struggled to find any rhythm.

Benfica's Brazilian coach Paulo Autuori attempted to give more pace to the midfield by substituting Valdo and fellow Brazilian Alexandre Amaral halfway through the second half but Porto were not to be denied.
Porto now have 41 points from 15 games, with Benfica second on 33 and Sporting third three points further behind.
Sporting had maintained their challenge for second place by defeating Estrela Amadora 1-0 away on Friday.

Benfica: 1-Michel Preud'Homme, 7-Jose Calado, 3-Jorge Soares, 5-Mario Bermudez, 17-Pedro Henriques, 30-Alexandre Amaral (Mauro Airez 81), 10-Valdo Filho (Ilian Iliev 80), 8-Joao Vieira Pinto, 21-Osmar Donizete, 29-Glenn Helder, 25-Martin Pringle.

Porto: 24-Henrique Hilario, 7-Sergio Conceicao, 22-Jorge Costa, 4-Aloisio Alves, 5-Fernando Mendes (Artur Oliveira 70), 17-Jose Barroso, 20-Paulinho Santos, 25-Zlatko Zahovic, 11-Ljubimko Drulovic (Joao Manuel Pinto 86), 21-Edmilson Pimenta, 16-Mario Jardel (Grzegorz Mielcarski 89).
